transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t seem to settle down inside myself anymore. It feels like I’m always needing to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m exhausted and I know I should just sit still. It’s wearing me out.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications, especially antipsychotics or antidepressants, in the weeks before this restlessness began?
I’m not sure. I don’t think there was any clear medication change right before it started, at least not that I can point to.
When you feel this restlessness, is it mainly a physical urge to move your legs or body that gets better once you actually get up and move around?
It’s not just my legs, no. It’s more like I can’t settle inside my own skin. I feel like I have to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m worn out and know I should just sit still.
Along with this restlessness, have you noticed changes in your mood, like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually elevated or irritable?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change like that—nothing I’d call unusually sad or really high. I do get frustrated with feeling this way, but I don’t know if my mood has changed beyond that.
Has this kind of restlessness and difficulty settling been something you've dealt with since you were a child, or is this a new feeling that started more recently?

It’s been around since I was a kid, honestly. Even in grade school, teachers would say I was bright but careless. I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work.
Do you find yourself frequently worrying about a lot of different things—like work, health, or relationships—more than you feel you should, and having trouble controlling that worry?
I don’t know that I’d call it a lot of worrying, no. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it being the main problem or something I can’t control.
Do you currently find it hard to stay focused on tasks, like reading, work projects, or conversations, because your attention keeps drifting?

Yes, I do. I can sit down with something simple, like the senior center newsletter or a choir schedule, and I start off reading it fine. But then after a few minutes I realize my eyes have gone over the same lines, and I don’t have any idea what I just read.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (childhood-onset) inattentive symptoms (careless mistakes, losing items, difficulty sustaining attention on reading tasks) combined with a persistent sense of inner restlessness and inability to remain still, present since grade school and continuing into adulthood, causing functional impairment (occupational/social tasks affected). No recent psychotropic medication changes or leg-localized urge relieved by movement to suggest akathisia or RLS. No pervasive worry or uncontrollable anxiety to support GAD, and no distinct mood episode to suggest a mood disorder. The chronic, developmental course with both inattentive and hyperactive-restless features across settings supports a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ICD-10 F90.0), Combined presentation.
